songs.title: High Score Summer
songs.style: Hazy electronic indie, psychedelic downtempo, 96 BPM. Same fictional artist: relaxed low grainy male vocal, close-miked, slight slapback, intimate unhurried delivery, no belting or falsetto stacks. Warm analog electronics, deep synth bass, tape character, dry drums, original melody. Loose swung drum-machine pocket, rounded repeating bass, soft electric-piano chords, sparse tremolo guitar and woozy synth haze. Warm afternoon feel, bittersweet but easy. Small melodic refrain, spacious verses, no stadium chorus, no EDM drop. A gentle instrumental turn after the bridge; resolved ending. No chiptune on this track.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The corner shop was closing
You had change enough for two
We took the long way to the arcade
There was nothing else to do
You balanced soda on the cabinet
And told me not to spill
I lost a life to make you laugh
I think about that still

[Chorus]
High score summer
Leave my name up on the screen
I don't need another number
Just a place we used to be
High score summer
Let the little green light stay
I was happy doing nothing
With you wasting half the day

[Verse 2]
The air conditioner was broken
Your hair was sticking to your neck
You drew a star upon my wrist
With a pen that barely worked
We never made it to the ocean
We could hear the traffic roll
You said the sea was overrated
Then you beat my highest score

[Chorus]
High score summer
Leave my name up on the screen
I don't need another number
Just a place we used to be
High score summer
Let the little green light stay
I was happy doing nothing
With you wasting half the day

[Bridge]
Someone's painted over the doorway
Someone's changed the carpet too
Every time I pass that corner
I still turn to look for you

[Final Chorus]
High score summer
Leave my name up on the screen
I don't need another number
Just a place we used to be
High score summer
Let the little green light stay
I was happy doing nothing
With you wasting half the day

[Instrumental Outro]

songs.title: Don't Pause Me Now
songs.style: Electronic indie dance, understated synth-pop accents, 119 BPM. Same fictional artist: relaxed low grainy male vocal, close-miked, slight slapback, intimate unhurried delivery, no belting or falsetto stacks. Warm analog electronics, deep synth bass, tape character, dry drums, original melody. Propulsive dry drum-machine groove, elastic syncopated synth bass, clipped rhythm guitar, warm analog chords. Short playful square-wave answer to the main synth hook only between vocal lines; 8-bit detail, not a game soundtrack. Verses stay close and loose, chorus becomes rhythmic and wider without glossy commercial-pop lift. Energetic night-drive momentum, brief half-time bridge, return to groove and decisive ending. No EDM build/drop, no sugary high tenor.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You keep your finger on the button
Like the room could disappear
I've been waiting for the right time
I've been standing here a year
Put your coat back on the railing
Let the phone ring in your bag
There's a beat behind the kitchen wall
I want to follow that

[Pre-Chorus]
We can talk about tomorrow
When tomorrow comes around
Let the record run a little
Let the needle wear it down

[Chorus]
Don't pause me now
I just got moving
Feet on the ground
Nothing to prove here
Let it run out
Let it go wrong
Don't pause me now
I'm already gone

[Verse 2]
All the plans we made on paper
Never made it past the stairs
Take the lift down to the pavement
Leave the list beside the bed
You don't have to call it freedom
You don't have to call it love
There's a light above the crossing
And it's green enough for us

[Chorus]
Don't pause me now
I just got moving
Feet on the ground
Nothing to prove here
Let it run out
Let it go wrong
Don't pause me now
I'm already gone

[Bridge]
Not a better version
Not a brand new life
Just a little motion
On an ordinary night

[Final Chorus]
Don't pause me now
I just got moving
Feet on the ground
Nothing to prove here
Let it run out
Let it go wrong
Don't pause me now
I'm already gone

[Instrumental Outro]

songs.title: Cherry Bomb Bonus Stage
songs.style: Playful electronic indie dance, leftfield synth-pop touches, 126 BPM. Same fictional artist: relaxed low grainy male vocal, close-miked, slight slapback, intimate unhurried delivery, no belting or falsetto stacks. Warm analog electronics, deep synth bass, tape character, dry drums, original melody. Short punchy arrangement, chunky syncopated synth bass, crisp dry drums, shuffled hats, wiry muted guitar. Occasional two-bar pulse-wave/chiptune fills and tiny coin-like synth blips between sections; warm 8-bit accents below the human vocal, never continuous video-game music. Hook is low, cheeky and rhythmic, not an anthem. Stop-start break before final refrain, short clean ending. Dusty tactile production, no EDM supersaws, no glossy chart-pop chorus.
